Base directory for this skill: /Users/michaelrihm/Documents/Projects/toolkit-v2/plugins/memory/skills/memory-save

# Memory save

Voice: write to the owner in plain English. Claude Code: follow the project's Plain English output style. Codex: follow the "How to write replies" section of `AGENTS.md`.
Saves, corrects, or retires one memory record with `toolkit memory` commands, or sends the fact to its proper home. It never edits memory files by hand.

## Steps

Track these steps in the host's plan tool (Claude Code: the task list; Codex: `update_plan`), not in the reply.

1. Decide the home with the memory criteria (`.memory/memory-criteria.md` with built-in memory, which wins; otherwise `references/memory-criteria.md`). Not memory: send it to its home ("Where other things go" below) and stop.
2. Search for a record that already holds it, and read each hit with its version. The save's duplicate check compares wording, so only this search finds a record the new fact contradicts (for example "Mondays" against "Tuesdays").
   `toolkit memory find '<topic>'`
   `toolkit memory get <key> --json`
3. Read the approval mode and apply "Approval policy" below. When it says ask, ask and wait.
   `toolkit config get memory.approval`
4. Write the description and body in the record format (`references/record-format.md`), then save with the form for the case ("Save forms" below).
5. Exit code 2 saved nothing. Read the "Error:" line. Records listed: the duplicate check. "Changed since it was read": read it again and redo the change. Any other rule: fix the text as the message says. `references/replacing-and-retiring.md`, section 2, has each case.
6. "Forget that": retire the record, with his words as the reason. Delete only when his own words say delete ("Approval policy").
   `toolkit memory retire <key> --reason '<his words>'`
7. An owner to-do with no work item, or a change to what is happening now: update the current focus (`references/current-focus.md`). A project term: update the glossary (`references/glossary.md`).
8. A preference a project setting can enforce (for example "I hate tabs" and `.editorconfig`): save it, then offer that change too.
9. Read the record back, check, and reply in one line ("Replies" below). End with the question still waiting for the owner, or the exact words that continue.
   `toolkit memory get <key>`
   `toolkit doctor`

## Approval policy

This is the only written copy of the memory approval policy.

- The owner's own words are the approval: "remember", "from now on", "always", "never", "forget", or a correction. Save now, with `--approved-by <owner>`. That includes a fact about a named person he asks you to remember ("remember that Priya's last day is October 15").
- `onboarding` mode (the default): something the agent inferred gets one yes-or-no line first, in exactly this form: "Save to memory: <one-line summary>?". Save after his yes (`references/proposals.md` when a proposal was saved for the question).
- `trusted` mode: a routine fact the agent is sure of is saved without asking and reported in one line, with no approver. The record says "Trusted grant".
- In either mode, always ask first for anything about a named person or personal details that he did not ask you to remember, for more than five records at once, and for a change to this policy.
- A delete needs his own words about that record ("delete it", "remove it for good"), or his yes to a numbered list that shows the delete. Do not ask again: the host asks him to confirm `toolkit memory delete`, and that prompt is the confirmation. "Forget that" is a retire, never a delete.
- A yes covers only the change and the meaning shown. Silence is never a yes.
- `--approved-by` is only for a change his words or his yes covered.
- An unanswered "Save to memory?" stays a proposal until he answers (`references/proposals.md`). Never drop it, and never save it with an approver.
- Only the owner switches the mode, in his own words ("you can save routine things without asking me"). Save his words as a `feedback` record with the date, then run one of:
  `toolkit config set memory.approval trusted`
  `toolkit config set memory.approval onboarding`

## Save forms

`<file>` is `-` in Claude Code, with the body on standard input after a quoted heredoc (`<<'EOF'`). In Codex give `--body '<text>'` in place of `--body-file <file>`. `references/record-format.md` shows both.

- A new record, from the owner's words or his yes:
  `toolkit memory save --type <type> --name <slug> --description '<one line>' --body-file <file> --source '<person or document>, <YYYY-MM-DD>' --approved-by <owner>`
- A new routine fact in `trusted` mode:
  `toolkit memory save --type <type> --name <slug> --description '<one line>' --body-file <file> --source '<person or document>, <YYYY-MM-DD>'`
- A question he has not answered yet:
  `toolkit memory save --type <type> --name <slug> --description '<one line>' --body-file <file> --source '<person or document>, <YYYY-MM-DD>' --proposal`
- An update of a record read in step 2, which his words or his yes covered:
  `toolkit memory save --type <type> --name <slug> --description '<one line>' --body-file <file> --expect <version> --approved-by <owner>`
- A routine update in `trusted` mode (the stored authorization is kept):
  `toolkit memory save --type <type> --name <slug> --description '<one line>' --body-file <file> --expect <version>`
- A new record that replaces an old one: add `--supersedes <old-key>` to a new-record form.
- A better name, or a type that matches the content:
  `toolkit memory rename <key> --to <new-key>`

## Gotchas

- Run each `toolkit` command alone, on its own line: never joined by `&&`, `;`, or a pipe, and never from a script. In Codex a joined command runs inside the sandbox, which blocks Hindsight, Notion, and the main checkout's `.memory/`.
- Put one-line values (`--description`, `--source`, `--reason`) in single quotes. An apostrophe inside them: Claude Code writes `'\''`; Codex writes ’ (U+2019) or rewords, and never uses `'\''`, which runs the command inside the sandbox. Double quotes run backticks and `$(...)`, drop that text, and the save still says "Saved".
- Never use a fixed file name such as `/tmp/memory.md`, and never write a file and run the command in one shell command.
- Body labels are bold paragraphs (`**Remember:**`), never `## Remember` headings.
- **Why** is the owner's reason in his words, or exactly "Not stated by the owner." Never a reason you inferred.
- In `onboarding` mode, a save with neither `--approved-by` nor `--proposal` is stored as "No approval recorded", and the save prints a "Note:" line about it. That is a mistake: fix it at once. Ask him, then save again with `--expect` and `--approved-by` after his yes, or with `--proposal` while he has not answered.
- A save of an existing key without `--expect` saves nothing. Take the version from the `--json` read; the first 12 characters are enough. Keep that read: its old text is the undo for an update.
- Add `--allow-similar` only after reading every record the duplicate check listed.
- A proposal the Stop hook saved holds only the one-line summary. His plain yes is `toolkit memory approve`, which takes out its "Do not rely on this" words; when he adds a reason or a detail, save the full body instead (`references/proposals.md`).
- Never store email addresses, secrets, or work-item status. The CLI catches common secret shapes, not all. For a secret, save where it is kept, never the secret.
- Ask the owner in the reply text, never through a question tool.
- Built-in memory: the CLI rebuilds `MEMORY.md` and repairs links in other notes after a rename, supersede, retire, or delete, and names each note it changed. Read that report (`references/memory-builtin.md`).

## Where other things go

| The owner's words are about | Home | Open |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Project work, a task, a bug, "add it to the backlog" | A work item | `work-on` |
| A decision for the whole project | `DECISIONS.md` | `work-decide` |
| A requirement for a work item | The item's requirements | `work-requirements` |
| Behavior already delivered | `requirements/` | none |
| How a change is built | The item's design | `solution-design` |
| Verified current structure of the system | `system-guide/` | none |
| Outside documentation | `ai-external-knowledge/` | none |
| A standing rule for how agents work here | A rule-file change, proposed to him | none |
| His to-do with no work item and no time | Current focus, Untracked to-dos | step 7 |
| A to-do with a time ("at 9 tomorrow") | A scheduled reminder, outside memory | the host's scheduling tool |
| A project term | The glossary | step 7 |

A short memory pointer to a hard-to-find record is allowed; never copy the record's body.

## Replies

Every memory reply ends with the next step: the question still waiting for the owner (for example "Save to memory: <one line>?"), or the exact words that continue. Never end on what was not done ("I haven't saved anything.").

- A new record: "Saved to memory: <title>. Say 'forget that' to undo."
- An update: "Updated in memory: <title>. Say 'undo that' to put back the old wording." His "undo that" is a save of the old text from the `--json` read (`references/replacing-and-retiring.md`, section 3). Right after a supersede, the undo is a restore of the old record and a retire of the new one (same file, section 4).
- A proposal: "Saved as a proposal for your yes or no: <title>."
- A rejected proposal: "Not saved: <title>. I will not suggest it again.", then the next step.
- A retire: "Retired from memory: <title>. Say 'bring it back' to restore it." His "bring it back" is the whole restore in `references/replacing-and-retiring.md`, section 7, not `toolkit memory restore` alone.
- A delete: "Deleted from memory, as you said: '<his words>'. This cannot be undone." For a secret or an email address, add that older backups still hold it (`references/replacing-and-retiring.md`, section 8).
- A failed save: lead with "Not saved: <reason>." Keep the text and try again later in the session. With Hindsight or Notion, the command prints the fix (`references/memory-hindsight.md`, `references/memory-notion.md`).

## Hook reminders

- The UserPromptSubmit hook adds one line when the owner's message holds one of six keep phrases: "remember that" (or "remember this"), "from now on", "don't ever", "note that", "going forward", or "keep in mind". It is a reminder: route the fact with step 1.
- The Stop hook blocks once when a keep phrase got no save, work-item change, or decision in the turn. Save it, or say in one line where it went instead.
- Ask in exactly the form "Save to memory: <one line>?" (bold is fine). Other wording, such as "Save it to memory?", makes the Stop hook stop the turn once and ask for that form.
- When a reply asks "Save to memory: <summary>?" and no proposal was saved in that turn, the Stop hook tries to save one, and the next turn's context says what happened:
  - It saved a proposal and names its key: his yes approves that key, his no rejects it (`references/proposals.md`, "Recording the owner's answer").
  - Memory already holds a proposal like it, and names it: his answer approves or rejects that proposal.
  - Memory already holds a record about the same subject, and names it: read it as in step 2. The same fact: keep it, or update it with `--expect`. A different fact and his yes: save it with `--allow-similar` and `--approved-by`. Never overwrite a record with a different fact.
  - The text looks like a secret, so nothing was saved: never save it; after his yes, save only where the secret is kept.
  - The save failed: save the proposal yourself in this turn, with `--proposal`.

## References

| File | Open it when |
| --- | --- |
| `references/memory-criteria.md` | Step 1, with Hindsight or Notion memory (built-in projects read `.memory/memory-criteria.md`) |
| `references/record-format.md` | Step 4: choosing the type and key, writing the description and body, passing text in each host |
| `references/replacing-and-retiring.md` | Step 5 (exit code 2), step 6, any update, supersede, rename, restore, or delete, and any undo |
| `references/proposals.md` | Asking "Save to memory?", a proposal named in the context, or the owner's answer to one |
| `references/current-focus.md` | Step 7: a to-do or a change to what is happening now |
| `references/glossary.md` | Step 7: a project term |
| `references/memory-builtin.md` | Built-in memory: links, the index, a link-repair report, notes the owner edited in Obsidian |
| `references/memory-hindsight.md` | Hindsight memory: a failed command, the server, how records are stored |
| `references/memory-notion.md` | Notion memory: a failed command, sign-in, Lore's layout, edits made in Notion |
| `references/examples.md` | You want a complete worked example of the case in front of you |
| `references/toolkit-commands.md` | A `toolkit` command fails, is refused by a hook, or you are unsure how to pass text in this host |

# Memory criteria

This file is the project-specific selection policy: what is worth keeping in lasting memory. The approval policy, including onboarding and trusted mode, is in the `memory-save` skill, which saves with `toolkit memory save`. When the owner corrects what is worth saving, save the correction as a `feedback` memory with `memory-save`, as a general rule, without copying the rejected memory. Those `feedback` memories override this page.

## Default test for lasting memory

Save a topic when it concerns this project, has a credible source, would matter in a future session, would be costly or unreliable to reconstruct, and has no better maintained owner. Prefer updating an existing topic. A short pointer to an authoritative record can qualify when future sessions would otherwise miss that record.

| Type and filename | Usually worth retaining | Route or reject instead |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `user_<topic>.md` | Relevant role, responsibility, working preference, or communication need the owner stated | Personal judgments, irrelevant biography, private details |
| `feedback_<topic>.md` | Repeated or standing correction to how the agent should work; confirmed selection lesson | One-off irritation, a rejected fact restated as policy, an instruction already in `AGENTS.md` |
| `project_<topic>.md` | Durable project constraint, rationale, technical landmark, or proven costly fix | A decision for the whole project (`DECISIONS.md`), code summary, schema copy, active ticket status, accepted requirement or design body |
| `reference_<topic>.md` | Hard-to-rediscover route to a source, system, dashboard, or decision record, with why to open it | Entire outside page or a path already obvious in `PROJECT.md` or the project map |
| `event_<topic>.md` | Significant project episode: what was done, what resulted, and where the output lives | Routine edit, tool call, raw error, daily progress log |

## Working context is different

`CURRENT_FOCUS.md` holds what is happening now: active work item IDs, what waits on the owner with no work item, untracked to-dos, and where the next session starts. It can change often. Keep a work item's detailed tasks and status in that item. Do not turn every open task into lasting memory. Do not discard an unresolved owner to-do merely to shorten the file.

## Never save as lasting memory

- Secrets, credentials, sensitive personal data, transcripts, scratch reasoning, raw logs, dropped guesses, or unsupported claims.
- A fact the same change already places in the authoritative file, unless a small route to that file is genuinely needed.
- Live status, pending approval, unshipped requirements, procedure steps, code restatements, or a current-system explanation that the code/System Guide owns.
- A rejected candidate under a new name or wider wording. A rejection stands until the owner changes it.

## Backup

This folder is Git-ignored. Back it up with `toolkit memory export --to <folder outside this project>` and restore a fresh clone with `toolkit memory import --from <that folder>`. Linked worktrees resolve to one vault in the main checkout. A fresh clone or machine needs its memory restored before the agent treats an empty index as evidence that no memory exists.

1	<!-- Generated file. Source: plugins/memory/shared/record-format.md. Edit the source, then run node dev/tools/sync-skill-references.mjs. -->
2	# Memory record format
3	
4	Purpose: the exact shape of one memory record (type, key, description,
5	frontmatter, and body), the same in built-in, Hindsight, and Notion memory.
6	
7	## Contents
8	
9	- Types
10	- Keys and file names
11	- The description
12	- Frontmatter
13	- Body
14	- Links between records
15	- What never goes in a record
16	- Passing the body to the command
17	- Checklist before a save
18	
19	The formats are the model project's: the topic template
20	(`.memory/project_topic_template.md`), `MEMORY.md`, `CURRENT_FOCUS.md`,
21	`memory-criteria.md`, and `terminology-glossary.md`. Only `toolkit memory`
22	commands write memory. They write the frontmatter from the flags; you write
23	the one-line description and the body.
24	
25	## Types
26	
27	| Type | Holds | Example key |
28	| --- | --- | --- |
29	| `user` | A role, responsibility, working preference, or communication need the owner stated | `user_plain_replies` |
30	| `feedback` | A standing correction to how the agent works, or a lesson about what to save | `feedback_no_force_push` |
31	| `project` | A lasting project constraint, reason, technical landmark, or costly fix | `project_deploy_window` |
32	| `reference` | A hard-to-find route to a source, system, dashboard, or record, with why to open it | `reference_backup_folder` |
33	| `event` | A significant project episode: what was done, the result, and where the output lives | `event_moved_off_heroku` |
34	
35	A type that does not match the content is fixed with
36	`toolkit memory rename <key> --to <new-key>`, never by saving a second record.
37	
38	## Keys and file names
39	
40	- `--name` is the slug: lower-case words joined by hyphens, short and
41	  specific, for example `no-force-push`. The CLI refuses a slug over 60
42	  characters; it never cuts one.
43	- The key is `<type>_<slug>` with every hyphen turned into an underscore:
44	  `--type feedback --name no-force-push` makes `feedback_no_force_push`.
45	  `toolkit memory save` prints the key it made.
46	- In built-in memory the key is also the file name without `.md` and the
47	  frontmatter `name`. The file name prefix and `metadata.type` always agree.
48	- Write a key with underscores everywhere: in `get`, `retire`, `restore`,
49	  `delete`, `--supersedes`, `--superseded-by`, and in a link. The CLI also
50	  finds a key typed with hyphens, but a link is text and must name the real
51	  file.
52	
53	## The description
54	
55	One line that a future session would search for. Aim for under 100
56	characters; the CLI refuses more than 150 and refuses more than one line.
57	
58	- Good: `Never force-push to any branch; use a merge or a new commit`

<!-- Generated file. Source: plugins/memory/shared/record-format.md. Edit the source, then run node dev/tools/sync-skill-references.mjs. -->
# Memory record format

Purpose: the exact shape of one memory record (type, key, description,
frontmatter, and body), the same in built-in, Hindsight, and Notion memory.

## Contents

- Types
- Keys and file names
- The description
- Frontmatter
- Body
- Links between records
- What never goes in a record
- Passing the body to the command
- Checklist before a save

The formats are the model project's: the topic template
(`.memory/project_topic_template.md`), `MEMORY.md`, `CURRENT_FOCUS.md`,
`memory-criteria.md`, and `terminology-glossary.md`. Only `toolkit memory`
commands write memory. They write the frontmatter from the flags; you write
the one-line description and the body.

## Types

| Type | Holds | Example key |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `user` | A role, responsibility, working preference, or communication need the owner stated | `user_plain_replies` |
| `feedback` | A standing correction to how the agent works, or a lesson about what to save | `feedback_no_force_push` |
| `project` | A lasting project constraint, reason, technical landmark, or costly fix | `project_deploy_window` |
| `reference` | A hard-to-find route to a source, system, dashboard, or record, with why to open it | `reference_backup_folder` |
| `event` | A significant project episode: what was done, the result, and where the output lives | `event_moved_off_heroku` |

A type that does not match the content is fixed with
`toolkit memory rename <key> --to <new-key>`, never by saving a second record.

## Keys and file names

- `--name` is the slug: lower-case words joined by hyphens, short and
  specific, for example `no-force-push`. The CLI refuses a slug over 60
  characters; it never cuts one.
- The key is `<type>_<slug>` with every hyphen turned into an underscore:
  `--type feedback --name no-force-push` makes `feedback_no_force_push`.
  `toolkit memory save` prints the key it made.
- In built-in memory the key is also the file name without `.md` and the
  frontmatter `name`. The file name prefix and `metadata.type` always agree.
- Write a key with underscores everywhere: in `get`, `retire`, `restore`,
  `delete`, `--supersedes`, `--superseded-by`, and in a link. The CLI also
  finds a key typed with hyphens, but a link is text and must name the real
  file.

## The description

One line that a future session would search for. Aim for under 100
characters; the CLI refuses more than 150 and refuses more than one line.

- Good: `Never force-push to any branch; use a merge or a new commit`
- Too vague: `Git preference`

## Frontmatter

The CLI writes it. Never write it by hand. A saved record starts like this:

```yaml
---
name: feedback_no_force_push
description: Never force-push to any branch; use a merge or a new commit
metadata:
  type: feedback
status: current
source: The owner, in chat, 2026-09-26
last_verified: 2026-09-26
authorization: Approved by Mike on 2026-09-26
supersedes: none
---
```

| Field | Holds | Set by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | The key | `--type` and `--name` |
| `description` | The one-line description | `--description` |
| `metadata.type` | `user`, `feedback`, `project`, `reference`, or `event` | `--type` |
| `status` | `current`; `needs-review` (also every proposal); `superseded` or `archived` for a retired record; `template` only on the seed template | `--proposal`, `retire`, `restore`, `approve` |
| `source` | Who or what said it, with an absolute date | `--source` |
| `last_verified` | The date the fact was last checked, or `unknown` | `--last-verified` |
| `authorization` | "Approved by <name> on <date>", "Trusted grant", or "Proposed by the agent on <date>" | `--approved-by`, trusted mode, `--proposal` |
| `supersedes` | The keys this record replaced, or `none` | `--supersedes` |

A save of an existing key keeps every field the command does not give again,
including fields another tool added. The CLI calls `superseded` and
`archived` together "retired" (`toolkit memory list --status retired`).

## Body

The body starts with a `# <Title>` line, then six labels, in this order, each
in bold at the start of its own paragraph. Never write a label as a heading
such as `## Remember`.

```markdown
# No force-push

**Remember:** Never force-push to any branch in this repository.

**Why:** The owner lost a day of work to a force-push on 2026-09-12.

**How to apply:** Use a merge or a new commit instead. If a push is rejected, pull first.

**Evidence and limits:** The owner, in chat, 2026-09-26. Applies to every branch, including work-item branches.

**Related memories:** [merge only by pull request](feedback_merge_only_by_pull_request.md)

**Authoritative records:** `DECISIONS.md` D-4; WI-012.
```

- **Remember:** one lasting point, or a few closely related facts, with scope
  and date where they matter.
- **Why:** the owner's reason in his own words, or exactly "Not stated by the
  owner." Never a reason the agent inferred: a later answer would present it
  as his. This is deliberately narrower than the model's topic template,
  whose prompt asks why losing the context would change future work. The
  rule came from the fixes after the sample runs.
- **How to apply:** what a future agent checks or does with it.
- **Evidence and limits:** the source with an absolute date (`2026-09-26`,
  never "today" or "last week"), and any doubt or limit.
- Write "None." after a label that has nothing. Never invent a related record
  to fill it.

## Links between records

- Link a related record with a relative Markdown link to its file name:
  `[deploy window](project_deploy_window.md)`. Never a `[[wikilink]]`.
- Link only when it helps a future session find the record, and check the
  target exists first (`toolkit memory get <key>`).
- Things outside memory (work item ids, `DECISIONS.md` rows, files in
  `requirements/` or `system-guide/`, tracker addresses) go under
  **Authoritative records** as plain text, not as links.
- Write the same links in every backend. The body text is the same
  everywhere, so a move between backends keeps them.
- The CLI repairs links to a record that is renamed, superseded, archived,
  or deleted, and names each record it changed. Read that report.

## What never goes in a record

- Secrets, passwords, keys, or email addresses. The CLI refuses the common
  shapes of a secret (an API key, a token, a private key, a password written
  out) in the description, the source, and the body, and an email address in
  `--source` and in the authorization. It does not catch every secret, or an
  email address in the body; those are the agent's job. When the owner wants
  a secret remembered, save where it is kept, never the secret: "The staging
  key is in 1Password under Staging".
- Work-item status, next steps, or unshipped requirements. The tracker owns
  them.
- A copy of a record that has a better home (a requirement, a design, a
  `DECISIONS.md` row). A short pointer under **Authoritative records** is
  allowed when a future session would otherwise miss that record.
- A fact the owner rejected, under the same or new words.

## Passing the body to the command

- Claude Code: pass it on standard input. Give `--body-file -`, then a quoted
  heredoc, then the body, then a line holding only `EOF`:

  ```text
  toolkit memory save --type feedback --name no-force-push --description 'Never force-push to any branch; use a merge or a new commit' --body-file - --source 'The owner, in chat, 2026-09-26' --approved-by Mike <<'EOF'
  ```

- Codex: give the body in single quotes with `--body '<text>'`. Newlines
  inside the quotes are kept. Write an apostrophe as ’ (the curly
  apostrophe, U+2019), or reword the text. Never `'\''` in Codex: the
  project's command rule does not match that form, so the command runs
  inside the sandbox, and the tool call can drop the backslash. For a long
  body, write a file with the file edit tool in a new folder made with
  `mktemp -d`, run the command alone with `--body-file <that file>`, then
  delete the file and the folder.
- One-line values (`--description`, `--source`) go in single quotes in both
  hosts. An apostrophe in them: Claude Code writes `'\''`; Codex writes ’ or
  rewords.
- Never write the file and run the command in one shell command, and never
  use a fixed name such as `/tmp/memory.md`.

## Checklist before a save

- [ ] The type matches the content (table above).
- [ ] The slug is short and specific; the key is not already in use for
      another fact.
- [ ] The description is one line a future session would search for.
- [ ] The body has the `# Title` line and all six bold labels, in order.
- [ ] **Why** holds the owner's words or "Not stated by the owner."
- [ ] Every date is absolute.
- [ ] Every link under **Related memories** points at a record that exists.
- [ ] No secret, email address, or work-item status.
